recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7890 unless FM opens a separate, broader issue about Claim prescription cardinality or line-level prescription modeling.
issue_request: FHIR-7890 was a Published/Persuasive FM clarification request asking the specification to elaborate the difference between Claim.prescription and Claim.originalPrescription. The accepted resolution asked to add an example where a pharmacy or other fulfiller supersedes the original physician prescription with an alternate medication of the same therapeutic intent; the fulfiller's replacement becomes Claim.prescription and the earlier physician order becomes Claim.originalPrescription.
initial_application: The clarification appears to have been initially applied in git commit 22d93a5dadf63d5f0ad563ac0560e61f03013e88, which added the example to the historical Claim spreadsheet source. Later source migration carried that content into source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml, with spelling corrected and the example represented as the Claim.originalPrescription comment.
additional_context: Claim is active in source/fhir.ini. Later related changes FHIR-17921 and FHIR-41258 changed the allowed target profiles for prescription/originalPrescription and already have audit commits on the combined branch; neither changes the intended distinction from FHIR-7890. A later Zulip implementers discussion about the same elements is consistent with the current source and no direct issue-key Zulip or Confluence conflict was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml already defines Claim.prescription as the authorizing document for services/products and defines Claim.originalPrescription as the prior prescription superseded by the current prescription, including the physician/pharmacy alternate-medication example requested by FHIR-7890.
